- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price increases (e.g., 80+ → 70s), then fail to correct downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model holds onto high forecasts longer than actual price declines.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent low prices — often delays correction until 10–15 days later.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days of the horizon, then gradually adjust downward — but too slowly.
- Model fails to account for sharp downward momentum after high peaks; often misses the “drop-off” phase.
- Overconfidence in short-term trends: forecasts ignore structural volatility or policy-driven corrections.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation of future values when prices are trending down.
